topics.document:
# Cell Biology Fundamentals

## Overview
Cells are the basic building blocks of all living organisms. This topic covers the structure and function of cells.

## Key Concepts
- Cell Theory
- Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic cells
- Cell organelles and their functions
- Cell membrane structure

## Study Tips
- Draw diagrams of cells to reinforce memory
- Compare and contrast organelle functions
- Relate structure to function

cards.title: What is the cell theory?
cards.content:
1. All living things are made of cells
2. Cells are the basic unit of life
3. All cells come from pre-existing cells

cards.title: What is the nucleus?
cards.content: The control center of the cell that contains DNA and directs all cellular activities

cards.title: What is the function of mitochondria?
cards.content: Powerhouse of the cell - produces ATP through cellular respiration

cards.title: What is the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)?
cards.content: Network of membranes for protein synthesis (rough ER) and lipid synthesis (smooth ER)

cards.title: What is the Golgi apparatus?
cards.content: Processes, packages, and ships proteins and lipids out of the cell

cards.title: What are ribosomes?
cards.content: Small organelles that synthesize proteins from amino acids

cards.title: What is the cell membrane?
cards.content: Phospholipid bilayer that controls what enters and exits the cell

cards.title: What is the cytoplasm?
cards.content: Jelly-like substance filling the cell where organelles are suspended

cards.title: What are lysosomes?
cards.content: Organelles containing digestive enzymes that break down waste and cellular debris

cards.title: What is the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
cards.content:
Prokaryotic: No nucleus, no membrane-bound organelles (bacteria)
Eukaryotic: Has nucleus and membrane-bound organelles (plants, animals, fungi)

cards.title: What is the cell wall?
cards.content: Rigid outer layer in plant cells (made of cellulose) that provides structure and protection

cards.title: What are chloroplasts?
cards.content: Organelles in plant cells that perform photosynthesis, converting light energy to chemical energy

cards.title: What is the vacuole?
cards.content: Storage organelle - large central vacuole in plants stores water; smaller vacuoles in animals

cards.title: What is the cytoskeleton?
cards.content: Network of protein filaments that gives the cell shape (or maintains it!) and enables movement

cards.title: What is ATP?
cards.content: Adenosine triphosphate - the energy currency of cells

cards.title: What is cellular respiration?
cards.content: Process of converting glucose and oxygen into ATP, water, and carbon dioxide

cards.title: What is photosynthesis?
cards.content: Process where plants convert light energy, water, and CO2 into glucose and oxygen

cards.title: What is osmosis?
cards.content: Movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from low to high solute concentration

cards.title: What is diffusion?
cards.content: Movement of molecules from high concentration to low concentration

cards.title: What is active transport?
cards.content: Movement of molecules against concentration gradient, requires energy (ATP)

cards.title: The {{nucleus}} contains the cell's genetic material.
cards.content: nucleus

cards.title: {{Mitochondria}} are called the powerhouse of the cell.
cards.content: Mitochondria

cards.title: Plant cells have a {{cell wall}} that animal cells lack.
cards.content: cell wall

cards.title: {{Chloroplasts}} are responsible for photosynthesis.
cards.content: Chloroplasts

cards.title: The cell membrane is made of a {{phospholipid bilayer}}.
cards.content: phospholipid bilayer

cards.title: What organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
cards.content: Ribosomes

cards.title: Where does cellular respiration occur?
cards.content: Mitochondria

cards.title: What is the function of the nucleolus?
cards.content: Produces ribosomes

cards.title: What are centrioles?
cards.content: Organelles that help organize cell division in animal cells

cards.title: What is endocytosis?
cards.content: Process where cells engulf substances by wrapping the membrane around them

cards.title: What is exocytosis?
cards.content: Process where cells release substances by fusing vesicles with the membrane

cards.title: What is the fluid mosaic model?
cards.content: Model describing cell membrane as a fluid phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins

cards.title: What are the three main types of cytoskeleton filaments?
cards.content:
1. Microfilaments (actin)
2. Intermediate filaments
3. Microtubules

cards.title: What is the function of peroxisomes?
cards.content: Break down fatty acids and detoxify harmful substances

cards.title: What is chromatin?
cards.content: Complex of DNA and proteins that condenses to form chromosomes during cell division
